visual_appeal: Reduce competing outlines: retain the outer frame and state rail, but replace internal gold panel borders with 1 px #443827 separators. The hero, instruction band, current-character strip and roster currently read as stacked boxes rather than one composed interface.

Give the hero's recommendation band a deliberate two-line hierarchy: 14 px primary action, 13 px follow-up, with 8 px horizontal and 6 px vertical padding. Remove the small outlined box around only the second step.
play_next_clarity: Make the primary instruction explicitly say 'Play Le Dette next'. Keep the prerequisite separately as 'Before switching: hearth Le Jette to an inn'. The current numbered band gives nearly equal emphasis to two different characters.
Change the follow-up to 'After Le Dette: Le Bankken, full in 19h 11m'. 'Then play Le Bankken' can imply an immediate switch rather than a future recommendation.
In compact mode, replace the unexplained run of state pips with grouped counts such as '1 full · 1 nearly full · 4 resting · 1 outside', retaining the required state colours.
state_colours: Keep all four state hues, but brighten the red progress fill to approximately #D45449 and the orange fill to #E69A32. The short red fill against the black well is noticeably less legible than the yellow and green fills.
Standardise state chips to a dark neutral background with coloured 1 px border, icon and text. The current large brown-orange chip backgrounds feel heavier than the full and nearly-full equivalents.
Use the same non-colour symbol consistently across roster, timeline and compact view: check for full, diamond for nearly full, moon for resting and warning triangle for outside.
character_identity: Increase roster portraits from approximately 42 px to 46 px within the existing 62 px rows; make secondary badges 18 px with a 1 px dark separation ring. Race/gender badges are currently too small to identify comfortably.
Move 'Account 3' out of the character-name line into a consistent secondary metadata slot. It currently competes with the identity rather than reading as provenance.

In the character card, align name, level/race/class, last seen and state chip to one left edge with 6 px vertical gaps. The speech and portrait are appealing, but the identity block feels loosely assembled.
default_theme: Lower the hero background artwork's contrast with a roughly 65% black overlay, especially beneath the metadata and progress bar. Keep the inn scene atmospheric rather than a second focal point.
Reduce the default theme's bright portrait surround to a 2 px gold rim plus the state ring. The current layered halo is substantially louder than the rest of the frame.

Use one button treatment throughout the default theme: 24 px height, 1 px #826632 border and restrained brown fill. The compact control, footer buttons and details action currently feel only loosely related.
elvui_wc3_fit: Match the reference windows' body font through the active skin's font configuration. The renders mix serif-like headings with a different body voice, while the supplied Character and Options windows have a much more consistent squared game-UI typography.

Use the skin's dark inset surface for roster and card wells, reserving warm brown for accents. The current large brown slabs sit less naturally beside the reference Character window's near-black interior.

Match title-bar height, close-button size and blue-button bevel to the actual skinned widgets rather than approximating them independently; the main window's tiny close control is particularly weak beside the reference windows.
alerts_ux: Fix the Esc-menu card overflow: 'Hearth to Feathermoon Stronghold, or find an inn.' extends beyond its right edge. Wrap inside a text region with 12 px side padding and reserve 24 px for the close control; grow the card vertically as needed.
Use at least a 24 × 24 px clickable area for every alert close control, while retaining the skin's visible X. Keep it 6 px from the frame edges.
Differentiate alert priority: reserve the red rail and warning icon for the logout intervention; use a quieter neutral rail for the rested-XP-used-up recommendation.
Clarify mover reset copy: use 'Reset position' on each placeholder and 'Reset all positions' on the control panel. Keep drag instructions inside the padded text bounds.
readability: Increase reading text to 14 px in roster metadata, timeline details and alert bodies, and use 15 px names. The nominal 13 px system still produces a visibly dense result; numeric compliance has not solved practical reading comfort.
Give time-to-full text a dedicated 22 px-high second line. Separate duration from calendar detail with a clearer delimiter, for example 'Full in 19h 11m · today 23:12'.

Do not truncate location names merely to preserve an old fixed grid. Allocate at least 270 px to identity metadata or move last-seen information to the character card before shortening the resting location.
Reflow Options into clearly separated groups with 20 px between sections and 24 px checkbox rows. Shorten the ElvUI frame override label and place its reload explanation on a separate secondary line.
layout_polish: Enlarge the NOW PLAYING strip from approximately 62 px to 76 px. Put the no-rested-XP message on its own aligned line rather than squeezing it into the middle of the identity-and-chip row.

Rebuild the hero action band on a stable grid: prerequisite left, primary recommendation beside it, details button right, future recommendation below. Give the final line at least 8 px bottom clearance.
Widen the timeline's after-48-hours column by 24 px and provide 8 px internal padding. Its dates and the outside-state explanation currently feel pressed against the plot boundary.

Replace the cramped footer sequence with two groups: account connection and sync status on the left, account filter and visibility control on the right. Maintain 16 px between groups and 8 px between related controls.
Apply measured text wrapping to every alert and card before finalising dimensions; the visible Esc-card overflow is a shipping blocker, not a cosmetic nit.
delight: Keep the character-specific speech, but visually connect it more clearly to the portrait: move the bubble tail toward the face and maintain at least 12 px separation from the identity block.
Make full-rest copy celebratory and useful: replace 'More rest is wasted.' with 'Fully rested — ready to adventure.' Keep the time-since-full information as secondary text.
Give timeline hover a crisp 2 px lane-start marker in addition to the broad highlight, so the fixed detail line has an unmistakable visual source without introducing a tooltip.

overall_notes: A meaningful improvement over the live baseline: the recommendation is prominent, roster columns are more disciplined, and the relative timeline with a fixed detail line is a strong decision. It is not yet a demanding-user approval. The largest remaining problems are dense reading surfaces, uneven hierarchy in the hero instruction band, and a plainly overflowing alert. The system needs content-aware sizing and stronger text hierarchy, not another isolated font-size adjustment. The supplied model-rendering limitation and narrower simulator fonts are not counted as defects; neither are the settled portrait rules or class-coloured names.
